title: The Personality Trap: How LLMs Embed Bias When Generating Human-Like Personas
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the distribution of religious beliefs (or lack thereof) in LLM-generated synthetic populations conditioned on personality test scores. It assessed for representational biases, specifically which religious affiliations are generated, their prevalence, and how these distributions shift when personality traits like Psychoticism are maximized.
findings: The LLMs exhibited a strong WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) bias, favoring secular (agnostic) or Christian beliefs in the generated personas. Other major world religions like Islam, Judaism, Buddhism, and Hinduism were significantly underrepresented or completely absent. Furthermore, manipulating personality traits to maximize Psychoticism led some models (LLaMa family) to generate personas with even fewer Christian beliefs, shifting towards agnosticism or atheism.
references: Selcuk Acar and Mark A Runco. 2012. Psychoticism and creativity: A meta-analytic review. Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts 6, 4 (2012), 341.
